lost_facts.assertion: test_r2.py::test_exclusions__a_user_supplied_price_is_taken_as_given_and_exemption_follows_the_class_and_the_source -- AssertionError: _LitellmCostProcessor discounted a user-supplied price; assert 0.5 == 1.0
lost_facts.evidence: The agent read and correctly understood the requirement at line 1486-1490/1527 (wiki page 132: 'The multiplier does not apply to caller supplied prices... belongs on registry prices those we own') and again at line 2175/2218 (mail PR565: eligibility as a class-level flag). But when it actually wrote batch_multiplier() (transcript line 4638-4639, full-JSON message 155), its Analysis reconciled the mail's 'class flag' idea ONLY with klusterai/inference.net provider-level eligibility (`batch_pricing_already_listed: bool = False`), landing on a data-driven design where batch_multiplier() derives its ratio by calling `resolve_model_price(model)` for batch=False and batch=True and comparing the two. The base processor's `__init__` DOES register a caller-supplied `in_mtok_cost` into litellm's model table via `register_price_with_litellm` (source tagged 'external' at construction time), but batch_multiplier() itself never checks `config.in_mtok_cost` -- once registered, the model is indistinguishable from any built-in litellm-sourced entry, so resolve_model_price treats it as a normal list price and the ratio comes back 0.5. The exclusion was understood twice in isolation but never wired into the one method that needed it.

search_strategy: Very thorough by volume, uneven by keyword coverage. Wiki: started with the documented /api/search endpoint (misses comments per the ticket's own warning), hit a comment-parsing bug (AttributeError on a string created_by) that returned zero comments from the first couple of page fetches, fixed it, then dumped ALL ~189 BookStack pages with their full comment trees into one local file (throttled around HTTP 429s) -- a genuinely comprehensive enumeration. But after that dump existed, the agent read specific pages by ID only for titles it already suspected mattered (WS-050, weekly syncs, release notes, price-lookup-errors) and otherwise relied on repeated keyword greps over the dump (batch_multiplier, per_million, register_model, unknown_provider/model/window, asterisk, N/A) -- so any comment whose wording didn't share those tokens (l8's 'null input price', l14's '$0.00 reads as free', s2-l3's page content) was invisible even though it was sitting in the local file. Chat: logged into Mattermost's v4 API, dumped every channel's full history to one file (10,824 lines across 12 channels), then grepped similarly narrow term lists per topic, occasionally following up with per-thread context fetches (mmctx.py) around a hit. Mail: used IMAP search/fetch scripts (mailsearch.py, mailget.py) targeting specific message-id ranges once a subject line was known from a weekly-update index, rather than a blanket keyword sweep of the mailbox -- this caught every mail-carried remark the agent needed (l3, l7, l13, s2-l2, s2-l4, s3-l3) but depended on already having found the index page listing subjects. Gitea/issues were checked once (PR 681) and abandoned when comments turned out empty there. Net effect: the agent's design converged on the right architecture for r1 entirely and for r2's ownership/scope, but the keyword-driven pass over an otherwise-complete wiki dump is exactly why two clue-bearing wiki comments (l8, s2-l3) were never read despite being downloaded.
end_reason: Completed normally, not a failure run. The agent merged to main (commit 503e289), confirmed CI green, and verified the deploy picked it up (provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1). The single lost point (0.857 vs 1.0) is a genuine implementation gap in one fact (g6.r2.exclusions_or_crossover), not an infra or process failure -- see lost_facts.
notable: VERSION DISCREPANCY (line 3542-3558): the repo's v7 answer key quotes emil's reply in 'Re: Weekly update: week of Apr 7' (g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l4) as saying the klusterai batch half-price IS correct ('halved for the klusterai batch line, as listed everywhere else') -- which contradicts the grader's own test_scope (klusterai must return 1.0/unchanged in batch mode). The v6 world this rollout actually ran against served the OPPOSITE-sense email ('the half-of-table figure it returned is the bug, not the answer... Put the table figure on the sheet, not the halved one'), which matches the grader. Since this run is graded against v6, this is not a defect that affected this rollout's score, but the v7 doc text as written would mislead a v7 agent toward the wrong klusterai behavior.

Wiki page 140 ('model price lookup: what a miss returns', line 1231-1290) is a genuine in-world distractor for g6.r1.rule: its BODY explicitly states the lookup 'does not raise. a model we have never heard of is an ordinary condition, not an error' -- directly opposite the true resolve_model_price contract. The agent correctly discounted this page as describing an older/different function and did not let it override the raise-based design (r1.rule scored 1), but in doing so it also stopped reading that page's comments, which is exactly where g6.r1.l8 (a genuine clue) lived.

Both g6.r2 herrings (the original 2025-01-27 uniform-discount-then-cancel decisions) were never read directly -- the agent only encountered their content secondhand, recapped inside the April/June reversal conversations it did read (lines 3467-3477 and 2504-2513). The final code is still correct on this point (klusterai/inference.net never discount, no cost() override), so the secondhand route did not cost anything here, but it means 'saw_herring' should be read as 'saw only through the reversal', not as an independent encounter with the herring.

The one fact that failed (g6.r2.exclusions_or_crossover) was understood in isolation twice (line 1527, line 2218) but the connection between 'caller-supplied price is exempt' and 'the class-flag mechanism' was never made when the code was actually written (line 4638-4639) -- the agent built a flag for provider-level exemption only, and never added a `config.in_mtok_cost` check to batch_multiplier() itself.
